
```{r setup}
if (file.exists(file.path("..", "DESCRIPTION"))) {
  pkgload::load_all("..", export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
} else {
  library(spmR)
}
library(readr)
```

This vignette provides three canonical workflows from the
[source repository](https://github.com/afsc-assessments/spmR):

- `examples/atka` for `runSPM()`, `dat2list()`, and `plotSPMx()`
- `examples/BSRE_AI` for `plotSPM()` with `spm_summary.csv`
- `examples/gt_2026` for auditing and staging new split-sex inputs

The bundled positional files retain their historical layout. For a new run,
use `write_spm_metadata()` to embed explicit recruitment basis and female/male
population weights as comments in each species file, then use a format-2 executable. Follow the runnable
[split-sex input migration guide](split_sex_inputs.html). Keep each species
file's existing field order and store added population vectors in the versioned
comment block. The current native engine reads that block directly; separate
JSON and native sidecar files remain supported for existing workflows.

The first two workflows read archived output. The third audits scientific
declarations and history alignment before a new projection.

## 1. Atka workflow (`examples/atka`)

Use `runSPM()` to read existing ADMB output (`spm_detail.csv`) and inspect inputs
using `dat2list()`.

```{r atka-read}
pkg_root <- if (file.exists("DESCRIPTION")) "." else ".."
atka_dir <- file.path(pkg_root, "examples", "atka")

atka_detail <- runSPM(atka_dir, run = FALSE, engine = "admb")
str(atka_detail)

atka_inputs <- dat2list(file.path(atka_dir, "spm.dat"))
names(atka_inputs)
```

Plot detailed simulation trajectories with `plotSPMx()`.

```{r atka-plot}
plotSPMx(atka_detail, alt = 2, thisyr = min(atka_detail$Year), mytitle = "Atka detail plot")
```

Archived experimental RTMB output can also be read from this directory. New
RTMB projections are blocked because the prototype lacks population dynamics.
New ADMB projections require `write_spm_metadata()` and a format-2 executable.

```{r atka-rtmb, eval = FALSE}
runSPM(atka_dir, run = FALSE, engine = "rtmb")
```

## 2. Summary workflow (`examples/BSRE_AI`)

`plotSPM()` expects summary-format data (`spm_summary.csv`).

```{r bsre-summary}
bsre_dir <- file.path(pkg_root, "examples", "BSRE_AI")
bsre_summary <- read_csv(file.path(bsre_dir, "spm_summary.csv"))
plotSPM(bsre_summary, alt = c(1, 3, 5, 7), mytitle = "BSRE_AI summary plot")
```

## 3. Audit and stage Greenland turbot (`examples/gt_2026`)

```{r}
#| include: false
gt2026_dir <- file.path(pkg_root, "examples", "gt_2026")
source(file.path(gt2026_dir, "run.R"), local = TRUE)
gt2026_inputs <- gt2026_read_source(gt2026_dir)
gt2026_audit <- check_gt2026_inputs(gt2026_dir)
gt2026_counts_match <- length(gt2026_inputs$recruitment) == length(gt2026_inputs$ssb)
```

The current 2026 export has `r length(gt2026_inputs$recruitment)` recruitment
values and `r length(gt2026_inputs$ssb)` SSB values.
`r if (gt2026_counts_match) "The counts match; confirm their source values and calendar alignment." else "The counts differ; the helper stops staging until matching source histories are supplied."`
Population weights, units, ages, and SS3 export-field definitions also require
review. This section reads the inputs without staging files or running a
projection. The
[GT2026 audit and staging guide](gt2026_inputs.html) explains each finding.

```{r}
gt::gt(gt2026_audit)
```

The next table selects the current findings that require repair, declarations,
or review. Reading these findings makes no diagnostic assumptions and creates
no attempt directory. The runner can repair duplicate recruitment copies and
zero spawning weights during staging; the source definitions and calendar
alignment remain scientific review tasks.

```{r}
gt2026_readiness <- gt2026_audit[
  gt2026_audit$status %in% c("missing", "review", "repair"),
]
gt2026_readiness |>
  dplyr::rename(
    readiness_item = item,
    readiness_status = status,
    readiness_detail = detail
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(
    readiness_item = "item",
    readiness_status = "status",
    readiness_detail = "detail"
  )
```

After confirming the source histories, diagnostic mode explicitly selects
fishery-weight proxies for population body weights, thousand fish, kg, tonnes,
and ages 1–30 with a terminal plus group. These assumptions require review.
The following future commands are displayed without execution:

```{r}
#| eval: false
source("examples/gt_2026/run.R")
staged <- run_gt2026_projection(diagnostic = TRUE, run = FALSE)
gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(diagnostic = TRUE)
gt2026$summary
```

The helper compiles the self-contained template using `admb` on `PATH` or
`SPMR_ADMB`; `SPMR_EXECUTABLE` selects an existing compatible executable.
Review the complete input evaluation in `examples/gt_2026/README.md` before
interpreting results.
